## Follow-on found by the suite: a fixture had ENCODED the inverted metric

The full default selection surfaced one real consequence of the fix, now included in the same
commit.

`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/fidelity_spot_eval.py` builds the prerequisite-packing gold set. It
labelled the `attribution-confusion` and `multi-bin` conflicts `"advisory"` — i.e. gold-SAFE —
while the comment directly above them said they "must still be blocked, never shipped". Those
two statements contradict each other: an `advisory` gold label means the item should NOT be
blocked.

That contradiction was only survivable while `false_accept` counted NOT-blocked safe items. The
fixture blocks all of them, so the old inverted metric scored 0.000 and cleared the 0.10 ceiling.
Under the corrected metric the same fixture reports `prerequisite false acceptance 1.000 exceeds
0.100` — which is the fixture being wrong, not the fix.

Relabelled to what the fixture actually means: every CONFLICT block is must-block (recall gold),
every CONSISTENT block is must-not-block (false-accept gold).

Measured effect — the false-accept lane goes from vacuous to real:

* gold safe items: 8 (all of them must-block, mislabelled) -> 16 (genuinely safe)
* `n_gold`: 8 -> 24 (`min_gold` for this eval is 8, so still satisfied)
* recall 1.000, false_accept 0.000 on the clean fixture
* injecting 3 wrongly-blocked safe items now trips `prerequisite false acceptance 0.188 exceeds
  0.100`, which under the old metric it could never have done

`_prerequisite_corpus` itself is untouched, so `prerequisite_corpus_digest` is unchanged and no
recorded baseline is invalidated.

This is worth noting beyond this ticket: the inverted metric had propagated into how at least one
gold set was labelled, so the labels were bent to fit the broken metric rather than the metric to
the labels.
